sources.note: VU Amsterdam's own 'Scholarships for incoming Master's students' page; contains the full VU Fellowship Programme (VUFP) and NL Scholarship sections, including eligibility criteria, funding amounts, application steps and deadlines.

awarding_body.detail: The page is VU Amsterdam's own site (vu.nl) and explicitly presents the VUFP as its own programme, funded by the university with support from VUvereniging.
awarding_body.quote: Our own VU Fellowship Programme (VUFP) is a merit-based tuition fee waiver. ... The VU Fellowship Programme (VUFP) is financially supported by VUvereniging: a social network of people who are connected to Vrije Universiteit Amsterdam.

deadline.detail: The page states the currently advertised cycle: Master's programme registration from 1 October 2026, VUFP applications from 1 November 2026, deadline 1 February 2027 (23:59 CET) for the September 2027 intake. This matches the record's deadline exactly.
deadline.quote: Applications are welcome from November 1st 2026. ... Deadline VUFP application: 1 February 2027 (23:59 CET)

eligibility.detail: Confirmed: the VUFP is for talented prospective non-EU/EEA passport holders who are not eligible for the lower tuition fee, applying to a full-time English-taught Master's at VU Amsterdam; the application steps state the applicant must already be conditionally admitted before applying for the VUFP; and applying for the VUFP automatically enters the applicant for the NL Scholarship with no separate application. Minor nuance noted: the eligibility bullet list says 'conditionally or unconditionally admitted' while Step 1 of the application procedure says 'you must have been already conditionally admitted ... before you can apply for the VUFP scholarship' - the record's claim follows the latter wording.
eligibility.quote: You hold a non- EU/ EEA passport and you are not eligible for the lower tuition fee. ... Please note that you must have been already conditionally admitted to the Master's programme before you can apply for the VUFP scholarship. ... When applying for the VUFP scholarship, you automatically apply for the NL Scholarship (formerly HSP) as well. No separate application is necessary.

funding.detail: The VUFP itself is a merit-based tuition fee waiver covering tuition fees only, with no living-cost allowance; it can be combined with the NL Scholarship, a one-time EUR 5,000 contribution towards living costs for which VUFP applicants are automatically considered. This matches the record's 'merit-based tuition fee waiver + living cost contribution' framing.
funding.quote: The VUFP scholarship covers the tuition fees only. It does not provide any additional allowance towards study or living costs, like rent, food, insurances. ... NL Scholarship is a one time contribution towards the costs of living of EUR 5,000 for the entire duration of your study period.

degree_levels.detail: The programme is for full-time English-taught Master's programmes at Vrije Universiteit Amsterdam starting September; it can be granted for one- or two-year Master's programmes. No PhD or Bachelor's offering.
degree_levels.quote: The VU Fellowship Programme (VUFP) offers talented prospective non- EU/ EEA students the unique opportunity to pursue a Master's degree at Vrije Universiteit Amsterdam.

recommended_field_updates.deadline_text: Applications are welcome from November 1st 2026. Deadline VUFP application: 1 February 2027 (23:59 CET)
recommended_field_updates.verification_notes: Verified live on 2026-10-12 against vu.nl. Cycle currently advertised: register for a Master's programme from 1 October 2026 (advised by 1 December 2026), VUFP application window opens 1 November 2026 and closes 1 February 2027 (23:59 CET), results mid-March 2027, acceptance deadline end of March 2027. Only non-EU/EEA passport holders who cannot pay the lower tuition fee are eligible; degree must not have been obtained in the Netherlands; students starting in February cannot apply; joint programmes not administered by VU Amsterdam are excluded. The VUFP covers tuition only - the EUR 5,000 NL Scholarship living contribution is a separate, automatic but not guaranteed award (around 20-25 per year). Re-check next cycle for updated dates and amounts.

notes_for_reviewer: The record's eligibility wording 'Must be conditionally admitted before applying' follows the application-procedure text ('you must have been already conditionally admitted to the Master's programme before you can apply for the VUFP scholarship'), while the eligibility criteria bullet list on the same page says 'conditionally or unconditionally admitted'. Worth flagging so the catalogue wording can note both. Also note some external scholarships listed on the same page still carry 2025/2026 dates (e.g. ASML, ECB, Jean Monnet) - those sections are stale but do not concern the VUFP itself.
